heard: a human sprint could launch you straight into orbit around Mars. In August 1877, astronomer Asaph Hall was ready to give up his search for Martian moons. His wife, Angeline Stickney, urged him to continue his search at the U.S. Naval Observatory. Hall discovered dimus, a smooth, dusty moon 12 kilometers wide that acts like a cosmic springboard. Its surface gravity is so weak that its escape velocity is only 13 miles per hour. That is slower than a fast human runner, meaning a simple sprint overcomes the moon's entire gravity.
